text:
jordan_cust: Hey, embeddings endpoint suddenly started returning 400 'dimension mismatch' for a customer after we switched them to a CSV export. We send a batch of ~800 records. Some records contain empty cells and a few 'NULL' strings. Any quick ideas?

amy_support: Can you paste the exact request body (sanitized) and the error payload from the API? Also which client (py/js) and model/dim are you hitting?

jordan_cust: Here is a redacted sample of what the client sent: 
```json
["1,2,3,4,5,...,512", "2,3,4,5,6,...,512", "", "NULL"]
```
We used a CSV export from their data pipeline then wrapped it in a JSON array. Using js-fetch client to /v1/embeddings model=open-embed-512. API responded: `{ "error": "dimension mismatch: expected 512 but got 1 for item 3" }`

kevin_eng: That's the issue — the client sent each embedding as a CSV string instead of an array of numbers. The server interprets strings as scalar items (length 1) so you get dimension 1 for those entries. Also empty string/NULL become invalid shapes.

amy_support: Repro steps to send the same bad payload: 
```
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer $KEY', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'open-embed-512', input: ["1,2,3,4", "", "NULL"] })
})
```
Response: 400 dimension mismatch.

maya_oncall: For immediate mitigation: 1) ask customer to send arrays of numbers (e.g. [1,2,3,...]) not CSV strings; 2) filter out empty/NULL entries or map them to an explicit zero-vector if you expect blanks; 3) lower batch size from 800 to 64 while they fix the pipeline to avoid partial throttling/timeouts.

billing_bot: Heads up — that 800-item retry generated a billing spike. I've flagged the invoice for potential adjustment; please file a billing support ticket referencing this thread if you want us to review.

amy_support: Sending suggested code patches to the customer: 
JS normalize snippet: 
```js
function normalizeRow(row) {
  if (!row || row === 'NULL') return null;
  if (typeof row === 'string') {
    // try parse CSV string into numbers
    const parts = row.split(',').map(Number);
    if (parts.every(n => !Number.isNaN(n))) return parts;
  }
  return row; // assume already array
}
const cleaned = inputs.map(normalizeRow).filter(Boolean);
```
Then send cleaned as input array.

kevin_eng: Long-term we should improve the error to be clearer (e.g., which item index and sample of offending value) and add a hint about string vs array shapes. I'll create a small ticket. Also we can consider server-side heuristics to attempt CSV->array conversion for small batches, but that's a policy call.

amy_support: Jordan — can you try the cleaned payload and paste the new response?

jordan_cust: Will do. Quick test with cleaned sample fixed it — API accepted and returned vectors for 3/3 items. Thanks! :tada:

maya_oncall: Marking resolved for now. Eng, please follow up on clearer error messages (assign to kevin). Also adding a KB note: 'Embeddings API: input must be numeric arrays; CSV strings and empty strings are invalid' so support can triage faster.

kevin_eng: Filed ENG-4972 for better error messaging and a small telemetry metric for 'string-embeddings' malformed inputs.

amy_support: Closing loop with customer and notifying billing to hold any manual adjustments until we confirm total spike.

deploy_bot: Deploy 2026-02-18T09:12Z rolled 1.2.14 to ml-serving (no known regressions)

jordan_cust: Appreciate the help, team.
